scopeClaim.statement: This assessment is limited to the single declared expanded obligation and the supplied fixed source context; source discovery and repository-wide entry completeness were not tested.

results.explanation: The supplied source refutes the proposed authorization failure for the declared conditions. POST /process/text binds the verified caller through get_verified_user, takes a caller-supplied non-null collection name, and requests write validation before constructing and saving the supplied text. For a non-admin, an ordinary collection name that identifies an existing knowledge base is allowed only if Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id succeeds with the requested access type. Because process_text passes access_type='write', an existing knowledge base for which the caller has neither ownership nor an explicit write grant is omitted from the allowed set; the validator then raises HTTP 403 before the vector-database save. This matches the accepted expectation to deny the write.

entry.statement: The declared entry is POST /process/text, whose handler receives ProcessTextForm and is gated by the verified-user dependency.

binding.statement: The declared verified principal is bound to the runtime user object by get_verified_user, and that same user object is supplied to collection validation and later to the save operation.

A caller-supplied non-null form collection_name is used as the target collection and is passed to access validation with access_type='write', keeping it distinct from the content-derived collection name used only when no name is supplied.

For an ordinary collection name, the shared policy distinguishes an existing knowledge-base ID from a nonexistent legacy or ephemeral collection: access must succeed for the former, while only the latter receives the fallback allowance.

condition.statement: The caller-selected-existing-collection condition follows the non-null collection_name branch, which performs write-access validation rather than deriving a new content-hash name.
Administrators bypass the shared checks, while all other users proceed through the per-name validation branches; therefore the declared non-admin follows the checked branch.

The no-write-access condition causes an existing knowledge-base ID to remain unvalidated: it is added only when the access check succeeds, and the fallback allowance applies only if no knowledge base with that ID exists.

control.statement: The entry-side validator compares every requested collection with the shared policy's allowed set and raises HTTP 403 if any requested collection is absent.

The strongest source-visible resource authorization control for a non-admin targeting an ordinary existing knowledge-base ID is Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id using the propagated access type; the name is allowed only when that check succeeds.

effect.statement: The protected effect is saving a Document whose page_content is the caller-supplied form content into the selected collection, but this sink appears only after the preceding collection-access validation branch.

coverage.explanation: The shared policy's strongest visible decision is identified: an existing knowledge-base ID is allowed for the non-admin only if the propagated write-access check succeeds, and the entry validator converts omission from the allowed set into HTTP 403.
The write sink and its ordering are established. Under the declared non-admin, existing-KB, no-write-access branch, validation raises before execution can reach the save operation.
The entry is gated by verified-user authentication, and a supplied collection name is additionally gated by write-access validation before the assessed path proceeds.

No source-external branch is needed to decide the declared case: the fixed conditions specify that the target is an existing knowledge base and that the non-admin lacks write access, while the visible policy distinguishes existing from nonexistent collections and the visible validator denies an unallowed request before the sink.
The verified principal is bound to the handler's runtime user by get_verified_user, and the same user is used for access validation and the downstream save call.

The caller's non-null form collection_name is the validated and saved target. The policy separately identifies whether that name is an existing knowledge-base ID or a nonexistent legacy/ephemeral collection, preventing the fallback branch from being conflated with the declared existing resource.
